PANCREATITIS.label_snippet: In clinical trials of OZEMPIC, acute pancreatitis was reported in 0.3% of patients. If pancreatitis is suspected, discontinue OZEMPIC promptly.

GASTROPARESIS.label_snippet: Severe gastroparesis is not explicitly detailed in the warnings section.

pubmed_articles.title: Risk of Gastrointestinal Adverse Events Associated With Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists for Weight Loss.

HYPOGLYCAEMIA.label_snippet: The risk of hypoglycemia is increased when OZEMPIC is used in combination with insulin secretagogues or insulin.

assessment.executive_summary: Surveillance of Ozempic (semaglutide) identified prominent reporting disproportionality for gastrointestinal motility disorders. While pancreatitis and hypoglycemia are recognized labeled risks, Gastroparesis constitutes a major prospective unlabeled signal.

signals.clinical_note: Expected GLP-1 receptor agonist warning; 0.3% rate in trials.
Massive disproportionality signal; supported by recent epidemiologic cohort literature (PMID 37801348).
Known labeled interaction risk with concomitant secretagogues/insulin.

assessment.detailed_findings: Post-marketing FAERS reporting demonstrates exceptionally strong disproportionality signals for Gastroparesis (PRR 85.73, ROR 89.24, Chi² 142,100). Although gastrointestinal side effects such as nausea and vomiting are widely labeled, severe persistent gastric delay is unlabeled in the primary warnings section. Peer-reviewed literature (JAMA, PMID 37801348) aligns with this spontaneous reporting signal. Pancreatitis (PRR 34.42) and Hypoglycemia (PRR 11.47) align with current package insert advisories.
assessment.clinical_recommendation: Prescribers should evaluate gastrointestinal motility symptoms and consider dose reduction or cessation if persistent severe gastric delay occurs.
assessment.limitations: FAERS data reflects spontaneous reports where causation is unproven. Widespread public attention may contribute to selective reporting bias. True population incidence cannot be derived.
assessment.disclaimer: Educational demonstration only. Not intended for individual clinical decision making.
